answer: Identity Decay Titration. Each identity carries a decaying verification pigment that fades with inactivity; reviving it requires paid recomputation whose price rises with how many dormant identities the same settlement layer revives in one epoch. An attacker cloning identities must continuously feed each one a pulse of activity or pay escalating revival costs across the whole cloned set. Cost scales superlinearly with clone count, since shared funding leaves a traceable relic tying dormant clones to one payer.
